frozen_original.title: Melania Appears in 209 Epstein Files Through Maxwell's Modeling Network
frozen_original.synopsis: The persons database in the Epstein Files reveals Melania Trump appears in 209 EFTA documents. Her connection runs through Paolo Zampolli's ID Models agency — the agency that brought Melania to the United States on a visa that, separately, was later found to have involved unauthorized early work. A 2002 email to Ghislaine Maxwell places the modeling agency network in Epstein's social orbit. Melania denied any ties to Epstein on April 9, 2026. The modeling industry connection between Maxwell's recruitment network and the agencies supplying young Eastern European women to New York's elite social circuit is a recurring thread across multiple Epstein victims' accounts.

primary.title: Report: 2019 FBI Proffer Included a Witness’s Claim About Melania and Epstein
primary.description_short: A report says a redacted former Epstein assistant told the FBI that Epstein introduced Melania and Donald Trump; the claim remains disputed.
primary.description_medium: An FBI proffer record from 2019 was reported to contain a redacted former assistant’s statement that Jeffrey Epstein introduced Melania Trump to Donald Trump. The report says the interview occurred in July 2019 and that the document is dated November 2019. The statement is an allegation, not an established account of how the couple met; public accounts described different introductions. The record does not substantiate the original 209-file count.
primary.description_long: In a 2019 FBI proffer, a redacted former assistant to Jeffrey Epstein said that Epstein introduced Melania Trump to Donald Trump. The Daily Beast reported that the witness made the claim during a July 2019 interview with FBI agents and federal prosecutors, and quoted the heavily redacted record as stating that Epstein introduced Melania to Donald Trump. The underlying allegation remains unverified. The article noted that the claim conflicts with Melania Trump’s memoir and with Donald Trump’s account, and reported that the Justice Department had warned that the file release could contain false or falsely submitted material. The FBI document is dated November 2019, while the interview is reported as occurring in July 2019. This is a separate, related file record, not a correction of the frozen entry’s distinct 2002-email date; that email item is omitted because the accessed sources do not substantiate it. This draft therefore centers the reported contents of one proffer and omits the claim that Melania appears in 209 EFTA documents, because the supplied record cites no verifiable count for that number. It does not infer knowledge, participation, or wrongdoing from a witness statement.

source_fact_map.fact: The report says the witness made the claim in July 2019.
source_fact_map.quote: made the claim in July 2019
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The unnamed woman, a former model who worked as Epstein’s assistant for a year from 2005 to 2006, made the claim in July 2019, three days after her old boss was arrested by the FBI and charged with child sex trafficking. The 11-page, heavily redacted document was published in Friday’s dump of three million Epstein files and uncovered on Monday. The woman’s claim contradicts Melania Trump’s memoir’s version of her meet-cute with her billionaire husband, as well as what he has said about how they became a couple. The White House pointed to a previous warning from the Department of Justice that the Epstein files may contain untrue information. The bombshell claim about the couple’s origin story appeared in an FBI record dated November 2019, which details a July interview with a woman whose name was redacted—and who was given immunity to speak. The interview was with both FBI agents and career federal prosecutors, and is recorded as a “proffer agreement.” Several lines of text were redacted before continuing: “ZEMPOLI was trying to buy Elite Models with EPSTEIN. EPSTEIN introduced MELANIA TRUMP to DONALD TRUMP.”

frozen_original.title: Trump Draws Electoral College Map With Sharpie to Inflate Victory
frozen_original.synopsis: Shortly after taking office, Trump reportedly showed visitors to the Oval Office a doctored Electoral College map drawn with Sharpie that expanded his red states to make his 2016 electoral victory appear larger than it was. The map was allegedly shown to visitors on multiple occasions as a prop demonstrating his historic victory. Election experts and cartographers noted the alterations misrepresented the actual electoral geography. The episode pre-dated the more famous Sharpiegate hurricane incident but reflected the same pattern of using a Sharpie to alter official documents or representations. The incident reinforced concerns about Trump's obsessive need to appear more successful than the actual record showed.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends Domestic Violence Programs at DOJ
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, the Trump administration eliminated all federal grant programs administered by the Department of Justice's Office on Violence Against Women, including grants that funded domestic violence shelters, rape crisis centers, legal assistance for victims, law enforcement training on domestic violence response, and prevention programs. Over $500 million in annual federal funding to thousands of community organizations that served domestic violence survivors was terminated. Domestic violence shelters across the country reported immediate funding crises, with some forced to turn away victims seeking emergency refuge. The National Coalition Against Domestic Violence warned that the cuts would lead to preventable deaths as victims lost access to emergency services, legal advocacy, and safe housing. The elimination was carried out as part of the broader DOGE-driven grant cancellation sweep.

primary.title: DOJ Withdrew Eight OVW Grant Notices and Later Reopened Funding With New Terms
primary.description_short: DOJ withdrew eight OVW grant notices in February 2025, then issued revised opportunities in May. The record documents a pause and reissue, not elimination of all OVW grants.
primary.description_medium: On February 6, 2025, the Department of Justice's Office on Violence Against Women removed eight listed grant opportunities and told applicants that the notices were under revision. The 19th reported no updated funding notices until May 7, after the original deadlines; three months later, six new opportunities appeared, only two corresponding to the withdrawn set. DOJ later announced 19 FY2025 notices. This was a pause and revised release, not the elimination of every OVW grant.
primary.description_long: On February 6, 2025, the Department of Justice's Office on Violence Against Women removed eight grant opportunities listed on its website and replaced them with a notice that applications were under revision. Reporting by The 19th, republished by Rewire News Group, said the office posted no updated funding notices until May 7, after the original application deadlines. Three months after the February removal, six new grant opportunities appeared, and only two were among those originally taken down. On May 23, the DOJ announced that OVW had released 19 notices of funding opportunity for FY2025 grants addressing domestic and dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. The revised notices included changed priorities and restrictions. These facts support a record about a temporary withdrawal, delay, and revised grant release. They contradict the frozen entry's claim that the administration eliminated every OVW grant program in February and terminated more than $500 million in annual OVW funding. The cited reporting describes uncertainty for applicants, but does not establish that all survivor services ended, that shelters turned people away, or that the entire annual OVW budget was terminated. The corrected account keeps the reported pause and reissue distinct from unrelated DOJ grant cancellations.
primary.subcategory: Federal grant administration and victim services

survivor_record.synopsis: The Trump administration is interfering in the 2026 midterm elections in an effort to entrench the imperial presidency. The administration is using a multipronged plan to subvert the elections and cement its power and policy agenda without accountability.
survivor_record.description_medium: The Center for American Progress argued that the Trump administration was using several methods to influence the 2026 midterms. Its fact sheet lists efforts involving election-denier appointments, federal voter data, agency cuts and executive orders affecting voting access. These are CAP’s claims and framing, not court findings.
survivor_record.description_long: The Center for American Progress published a fact sheet on August 19, 2026, arguing that the Trump administration was using a multipronged strategy to shape the 2026 midterm elections. Its examples included public claims casting doubt on election integrity, appointments of election deniers to federal roles, cuts to agencies and election-security programs, demands for voter information from states, and executive orders aimed at voting procedures. The organization also warned about possible federal pressure on election certification. CAP presented these measures as a coordinated effort to consolidate power, so that interpretation should be attributed to the advocacy group rather than treated as an adjudicated finding. The fact sheet identifies concrete policy actions and proposals behind its concern, giving the record more substance than a general claim of interference. It does not establish that every measure would alter election results, that all described actions were implemented, or that a court had found the administration violated election law. The sourced account is therefore a report of CAP’s allegations and examples, with the legal and electoral effects left open.
